- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong downward momentum, model often overshoots downward; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overreacts and forecasts a prolonged rally; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward bias if price has been above 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early decline (first 5–7 days), model often misses it; apply a 1–3% downward correction in first 3–5 days of forecast.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to underreact; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to counteract underestimation.
